author_or_institution: Fortune (reporting on Erik Brynjolfsson and ADP Research)
title: 'It's not going away': The Stanford economist who called the AI entry-level jobs crisis early has the receipts
claim_or_use: ADP 'Canaries Dashboard' payroll data showing employment for workers 22-25 in highly AI-exposed occupations shrinking at roughly 3.8% per year, versus growth in the least-exposed jobs for the same age group
notes: Describes the June 2026 update to the original August 2025 Brynjolfsson/ADP working paper; figures are from ADP payroll data covering roughly one-sixth of the U.S. workforce.

title: Anthropic Economic Index report: Learning curves
claim_or_use: Which tasks and occupations show measurable Claude usage, and how usage concentration has changed between January 2025 and February 2026
notes: First-party report on aggregated, anonymized Claude.ai and API usage; not independently audited.

title: Labor market impacts of AI: A new measure
claim_or_use: No clear unemployment signal in high-exposure occupations as of early 2026, but roughly 14% slower relative hiring of workers aged 22-25 into the most AI-exposed roles
notes: Anthropic's own labor-market analysis; a single company's usage data is not a full labor-market census.

title: Time, Work-Discipline, and Industrial Capitalism
claim_or_use: Historical account of the shift from task-oriented to clock-disciplined, wage-based labor during industrialization
notes: Past & Present, Vol. 38, No. 1, pp. 56-97. Foundational labor-history source; used for the historical framing only, not as commentary on AI.

title: How Company Culture Shapes Employee Motivation
claim_or_use: Original statement of the six motives that drive work: play, purpose, and potential as direct motives; emotional pressure, economic pressure, and inertia as indirect motives
notes: Companion article to the authors' book Primed to Perform; summarizes the 'why we work determines how well we work' argument.

title: Primed to Perform: How to Build the Highest Performing Cultures Through the Science of Total Motivation
claim_or_use: Full statement and case-study application of the Total Motivation (ToMo) framework across organizations including Apple, Starbucks, and Southwest Airlines
notes: HarperBusiness, 2015. The authors are former McKinsey consultants and founders of Vega Factor; the proprietary ToMo survey methodology is not independently peer-reviewed.

title: Introduction to Drive: The Surprising Truth About What Motivates Us
claim_or_use: Secondary retelling of Harry Harlow's 1949 rhesus-monkey puzzle-box experiments and their challenge to behaviorist drive-reduction theory
notes: Secondary source; used because Harlow's original 1950 Journal of Comparative and Physiological Psychology paper is not freely accessible, and Pink's retelling is the standard popular reference point. Flagged as secondary in-text.

title: How a 1949 monkey experiment showed us how wrong we were about what motivates us
claim_or_use: Additional detail on Harlow's experimental design (eight rhesus monkeys, mechanical puzzles, two-week observation) and the finding that adding food rewards made performance worse
notes: Secondary popular account; cross-checked against Pink's retelling for consistency before use.

title: Motivation Reconsidered: The Concept of Competence
claim_or_use: Introduces 'effectance motivation' — a proposed drive toward competent interaction with the environment, offered as a bridge between Harlow-style curiosity findings and a more general theory of intrinsic motivation
notes: Psychological Review, 66, pp. 297-333. Influential precursor to self-determination theory's concept of competence, covered in Chapter 7.

author_or_institution: Richard M. Ryan; Wendy S. Grolnick (eds.)
title: reprinting Edward L. Deci
source_type: Beyond Reinforcement: Deci (1971) on the Effects of Rewards on Self-Determination
claim_or_use: Retrospective academic reprint/commentary
url: Design and findings of Deci's original 1971 Soma-cube experiment: paid participants spent less free-choice time on the puzzle than unpaid participants
notes: https://selfdeterminationtheory.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/2019_RyanRyanDiDomencio_Deci1971.pdf
column11: Hosted by the Center for Self-Determination Theory; includes direct discussion of the original 1971 Journal of Personality and Social Psychology study.

author_or_institution: Mark R. Lepper; David Greene; Richard E. Nisbett
title: Undermining Children's Intrinsic Interest with Extrinsic Reward: A Test of the 'Overjustification' Hypothesis
claim_or_use: Original 'Good Player Award' preschool study: children who expected a reward for drawing later showed less free-time interest in drawing than children who received no reward or an unexpected one
notes: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 1973, Vol. 28, No. 1, pp. 129-137. Sample of 51 preschool children; effect specific to expected, task-contingent rewards.

author_or_institution: Edward L. Deci; Richard Koestner; Richard M. Ryan
title: A Meta-Analytic Review of Experiments Examining the Effects of Extrinsic Rewards on Intrinsic Motivation
claim_or_use: 128-experiment meta-analysis concluding that tangible, expected, task-contingent rewards significantly and substantially undermine intrinsic motivation, rebutting Cameron and Pierce's 1994 meta-analysis, which had concluded the effect was limited
notes: Psychological Bulletin, 125(6), pp. 627-668. Part of a sustained academic controversy; Eisenberger, Pierce, and Cameron published a rebuttal the same year, and the exchange continued in subsequent issues of the journal.

title: Flow: The Psychology of Optimal Experience
claim_or_use: Definition and structural conditions of flow: clear goals, immediate feedback, and a balance between perceived challenge and skill
notes: Harper & Row, 1990. URL is a secondary topic overview used to confirm the standard summary of the theory's core conditions alongside the book itself.

title: Componential Theory of Creativity
claim_or_use: Amabile's componential model: domain-relevant skills, creativity-relevant processes, and intrinsic task motivation, shaped by the social environment, as joint determinants of creative output
notes: Harvard Business School Working Paper 12-096; updates Amabile's original 1983 formulation of the theory.

author_or_institution: Richard M. Ryan and Edward L. Deci
title: Self-Determination Theory and the Facilitation of Intrinsic Motivation, Social Development, and Well-Being
claim_or_use: Statement of self-determination theory's three basic psychological needs: autonomy, competence, and relatedness
notes: American Psychologist, 55(1), 68-78. One of the most cited papers in modern psychology.

title: Self-determination theory and the facilitation of intrinsic motivation
claim_or_use: and well-being
notes: Confirms full bibliographic citation and abstract for Ryan and Deci (2000)
column12: Used only to verify citation accuracy.

author_or_institution: Paul P. Baard; Edward L. Deci; Richard M. Ryan
title: Intrinsic Need Satisfaction: A Motivational Basis of Performance and Well-Being in Two Work Settings
claim_or_use: Field study of 124 executives at a Fortune 500 company finding that managerial autonomy support predicted employees' satisfaction of autonomy, competence, and relatedness needs, which in turn predicted performance evaluations and psychological adjustment
notes: Journal of Applied Social Psychology, 34(10), pp. 2045-2068. One of the more direct applications of self-determination theory to a corporate performance-evaluation setting.

title: Self-Determination Theory and Work Motivation
claim_or_use: Comprehensive review applying self-determination theory to organizational behavior; later recognized by the Journal of Organizational Behavior as one of its eight most influential articles
notes: Journal of Organizational Behavior, 26, pp. 331-362.

title: The Future of Jobs Report 2025
claim_or_use: Projection of 170 million new roles created and 92 million displaced by 2030, a net gain of 78 million jobs, with about 22% of current jobs subject to disruption and roughly 39% of required skills changing within five years
notes: Survey-based projection from employers representing a large share of the global workforce; a projection, not a realized outcome, and should be labeled as such.

author_or_institution: Fortune (reporting on Erik Brynjolfsson and ADP Research)
title: 'It's not going away': The Stanford economist who called the AI entry-level jobs crisis early has the receipts
claim_or_use: Detailed breakdown of which task types (information retrieval, summarization, scheduling, formatting, routine drafting) are being absorbed first and assigned historically to junior employees
notes: Same source as ch01-001, cited again here for its task-level detail.

title: Anthropic Economic Index report: Learning curves
claim_or_use: 49% of jobs in Anthropic's sample had Claude used for at least a quarter of their tasks by February 2026, up from 36% a year earlier; only 7.5% of O*NET tasks overall show measurable usage
notes: Same source as ch01-002; adoption remains concentrated rather than uniform across the full task taxonomy.

title: Unemployment Rate for Recent College Graduates Holds at 5.6%
claim_or_use: Business journalism
url: Recent-graduate unemployment (ages 22-27, bachelor's degree) at 5.6% versus 4.2% for all workers as of early 2026 — the widest gap on record in New York Fed data
notes: https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-05-05/unemployment-for-recent-college-grads-remains-high-ny-fed-says
column11: Reporting on the Federal Reserve Bank of New York's Labor Market for Recent College Graduates series.

author_or_institution: Federal Reserve Bank of New York
title: The Labor Market for Recent College Graduates
claim_or_use: First-party source for recent-graduate versus all-worker unemployment and underemployment rates
notes: Updated quarterly; figures cited in the chapter reflect the early-2026 snapshot and will move over time.

author_or_institution: Randal S. Olson (summarizing New York Fed research)
title: New U.S. college grads now have higher unemployment than the average worker
claim_or_use: New York Fed's own analysis attributing roughly 64% of the rise in young-graduate unemployment to remote-work-driven hiring caution rather than AI directly
notes: Used deliberately as counter-evidence against an overly simple 'AI did this' reading of the graduate unemployment data.

title: Robots and Jobs: Evidence from US Labor Markets
claim_or_use: Each additional robot per thousand workers in a U.S. commuting zone reduced the local employment-to-population ratio by about 0.2 percentage points and wages by about 0.42%, concentrated in manufacturing and routine blue-collar occupations
notes: Journal of Political Economy, 128(6), 2020. Cited as a contrasting historical precedent (physical robotic automation, blue-collar concentration) rather than a direct analogue to cognitive-task AI substitution.

author_or_institution: Guido W. Imbens; Donald B. Rubin; Bruce I. Sacerdote
title: Estimating the Effect of Unearned Income on Labor Earnings, Savings, and Consumption: Evidence from a Survey of Lottery Players
claim_or_use: Massachusetts lottery-winner survey: large-prize winners modestly reduced work hours and earnings and increased big-ticket spending; small and medium winners changed little
notes: Published version in American Economic Review 91(4), 2001. Survey-based, mid-1980s Massachusetts lottery players.

author_or_institution: David Cesarini; Erik Lindqvist; Matthew J. Notowidigdo; Robert Östling
title: The Effect of Wealth on Individual and Household Labor Supply: Evidence from Swedish Lotteries
claim_or_use: Randomized Swedish lottery-prize evidence that wealth modestly and persistently reduces earnings, with a stronger effect for winners than their spouses
notes: American Economic Review 107(12), 2017, pp. 3917-3946.

author_or_institution: Philip Brickman; Dan Coates; Ronnie Janoff-Bulman
title: Lottery Winners and Accident Victims: Is Happiness Relative?
claim_or_use: 22 major lottery winners were not happier on average than controls and reported less pleasure from mundane events; basis of the 'happiness set point' and adaptation-level literature
notes: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 36, pp. 917-927. Small sample (22 winners, 22 controls, 29 accident victims); a foundational but dated study.

title: The Association of Retirement Age with Mortality: A Population-Based Longitudinal Study among Older Adults in the United States
claim_or_use: U.S. longitudinal evidence bearing on whether later retirement is associated with lower all-cause mortality
notes: One study among several with mixed findings; used alongside the 'healthy worker effect' caveat rather than as a standalone verdict.

title: Health status of workers approximately 60 years of age and the risk of early death after compulsory retirement: A cohort study
claim_or_use: Evidence on the 'healthy worker effect': people who can afford early retirement are systematically healthier and wealthier, confounding naive retirement-mortality comparisons
notes: Used to explain why cross-sectional retirement-mortality comparisons are unreliable without adjustment.

title: The Busy Ethic: Moral Continuity Between Work and Retirement
claim_or_use: Concept of the 'busy ethic': retirees legitimize leisure by keeping it earnest, active, and occupied, preserving continuity with the work ethic rather than rejecting it
notes: The Gerontologist, 26(3), pp. 239-244.

author_or_institution: Finnish Ministry of Social Affairs and Health / Prime Minister's Office
title: Preliminary results of the basic income experiment: self-perceived wellbeing improved
source_type: during the first year no effects on employment
claim_or_use: Government report
url: 2017-2018 two-year Finnish basic-income trial: 2,000 unemployed recipients of a 560-euro monthly unconditional payment; small employment effects, clearer improvements in self-reported wellbeing and reduced mental strain
notes: https://valtioneuvosto.fi/en/article/-/asset_publisher/1271139/perustulokokeilun-alustavat-tulokset-hyvinvointi-koettiin-paremmaksi-ensimmaisena-vuonna-ei-tyollisyysvaikutuksia
column11: First-party Finnish government release of the trial's preliminary results.

author_or_institution: Finnish Ministry of Social Affairs and Health
title: Results of the basic income experiment: small employment effects
source_type: better perceived economic security and mental wellbeing
claim_or_use: Government report
url: Final-year results confirming modest employment effects (about six additional days of employment on average) and stronger wellbeing effects
notes: https://stm.fi/en/-/perustulokokeilun-tulokset-tyollisyysvaikutukset-vahaisia-toimeentulo-ja-psyykkinen-terveys-koettiin-paremmaksi
column11: Companion release to ch12-001 covering the full two-year period; notes that a concurrent activation-model policy change complicates interpretation of the employment figures.

title: Early findings from the world's largest UBI study
claim_or_use: Kenya long-horizon UBI study design: roughly 23,000 recipients across 195 villages, comparing lump-sum, two-year, and twelve-year transfer arms
notes: First-party organizational summary of an independently run randomized evaluation; should be read alongside the academic evaluation for methodological detail.

title: It's one of the biggest experiments in fighting global poverty. Now
claim_or_use: Public radio journalism
url: Kenya UBI findings that the two-year-only arm underperformed the lump-sum and twelve-year arms on several economic measures despite similar cumulative transfers, with growth concentrated in non-agricultural enterprise formation
notes: https://www.npr.org/sections/goatsandsoda/2023/12/07/1217478771/its-one-of-the-biggest-experiments-in-fighting-global-poverty-now-the-results-ar
column11: Independent journalistic account drawing on the academic working paper behind the GiveDirectly-funded study.

title: The Effects of a Universal Basic Income in Kenya
claim_or_use: Confirms study design and headline findings of the randomized Kenya UBI evaluation, including the shift in labor supply from wage employment toward self-employment
notes: Independent research-partner summary, used to cross-check the GiveDirectly first-party account.

title: Scarcity: Why Having Too Little Means So Much
source_type: Trade nonfiction book (drawing on peer-reviewed research)
claim_or_use: Scarcity imposes a cognitive 'bandwidth tax' and produces 'tunneling' toward immediate demands at the expense of longer-horizon planning, offering a psychological mechanism for why short-horizon income guarantees underperform long-horizon ones
notes: Times Books/Henry Holt, 2013. Synthesizes the authors' own peer-reviewed experimental and field research; used here as a plausible explanatory mechanism, not as direct evidence about either the Finland or Kenya trial specifically.

title: The 'Resting' Generation and South Korea's Youth Recession
claim_or_use: South Korean youth (ages 15-29) employment rate falling to 44.3%, with roughly 470,000 young Koreans classified as 'resting' — neither employed nor seeking work
notes: 2026 update on the longer-running 'sampo generation' phenomenon; distinguishes unemployment from labor-force withdrawal.

title: Miracle under threat: South Korea's birth rate collapse could undo decades of growth
claim_or_use: South Korea's birth rate near 0.9 and demographic-decline context for the youth labor-market and marriage-and-childbearing retreat described as the 'sampo' pattern
notes: Used for demographic and economic context, not as a labor-market data source in itself.

title: Low Youth Employment in Korea Part 1: The 'Golden Ticket Syndrome'
claim_or_use: Structural explanation of Korean youth labor-market dysfunction: credentialism, intense competition for a narrow band of large-firm jobs, and resulting underemployment and withdrawal
notes: Used for institutional and structural context distinct from any AI-displacement mechanism.

title: Survey Findings Suggest Japan Has More than 1 Million 'Hikikomori'
claim_or_use: 2022 Japan Cabinet Office survey estimating roughly 1.46 million people across all ages, about 2% of the population, meeting hikikomori criteria
notes: First nationwide, all-age Cabinet Office survey of hikikomori, conducted in 2022.

title: Supporting Japanese people affected by severe social isolation: A case study
claim_or_use: Policy response context, including Japan's 2021 appointment of a Minister for Social Isolation and Loneliness and 2024 loneliness law
notes: International-organization case study used for policy-response detail.

title: 2% of Japanese Labour Force Could Be 'Modern-day Recluses': Government Survey
claim_or_use: Additional detail and commentary on the 2022 Cabinet Office survey's findings and definitional boundaries
notes: Used to cross-check the Nippon.com figures.

title: Rising morbidity and mortality in midlife among white non-Hispanic Americans in the 21st century
claim_or_use: Original 'deaths of despair' finding: reversal of expected mortality declines among midlife white non-Hispanic Americans, driven by suicide, drug and alcohol poisoning, and chronic liver disease
notes: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 2015. Landmark, widely cited, and also widely contested finding.

title: Education
claim_or_use: and Death
notes: Extension of the deaths-of-despair finding along educational-attainment lines, and the authors' account of its relationship to labor-market and community decline
column12: Later working paper extending the original 2015 PNAS study; companion to the authors' 2020 book Deaths of Despair and the Future of Capitalism.

title: Deaths of Despair in Comparative Perspective
claim_or_use: Independent scholarly review assessing competing explanations for deaths-of-despair trends, including opioid-supply and regional-economic-decline accounts
notes: Used specifically as the chapter's counter-evidence and scientific-controversy source.

title: State of the Global Workplace 2026
claim_or_use: Global employee engagement at 20% in 2025, down from a 2022 peak of 23%, with two consecutive years of decline and no region increasing engagement
notes: Gallup's annual flagship workplace report; figures are survey-based estimates, not a census.

title: The Great Detachment: Why Employees Feel Stuck
claim_or_use: 'Great Detachment' framing: record-low employee satisfaction and connection to company mission (down from 38% in 2021 to a low of 30% in 2024) combined with employees' reduced ability to find new jobs in a cooling market
notes: First-party Gallup analysis; survey conducted Oct 23-Nov 5, 2024, with 22,558 employees.

title: What is Quiet Quitting And Why Is It Happening
claim_or_use: Origin of 'quiet quitting' in a July 25, 2022 TikTok video by Zaid Khan, and its rapid spread into mainstream workplace discourse
notes: Used for the term's documented origin and early framing.

title: The economics behind 'quiet quitting' — and what we should call it instead
claim_or_use: Economic framing of quiet quitting as reduced discretionary effort rather than literal resignation, and Gallup's contemporaneous engagement data
notes: Used for economic context and Gallup's early response to the phenomenon.

title: Job openings and quits reach record highs in 2021
source_type: layoffs and discharges fall to record lows
claim_or_use: Official government data report
url: Quits rate reaching a then-record 3.0% in November-December 2021, and 4.5 million voluntary quits in November 2021 alone, as the peak-visibility contrast to later disengagement trends
notes: https://www.bls.gov/opub/mlr/2022/article/job-openings-and-quits-reach-record-highs-in-2021.htm
column11: Monthly Labor Review; official JOLTS-derived figures.

title: Cambridge University
claim_or_use: The results are in: the UK's four-day week pilot
notes: UK 2022 pilot (61 companies, ~2,900 workers): revenue roughly stable and up about 35% year-over-year across the trial group, staff turnover down 57%, and 71% of employees reporting reduced burnout
column12: Coordinated by 4 Day Week Global with researchers including Professor Juliet Schor of Boston College.

title: Making It Stick: The UK Four-Day Week Pilot One Year On
claim_or_use: One-year follow-up: 56 of 61 companies (92%) retained the four-day week, 18 made it permanent, and roughly a third reported improved recruitment
notes: Follow-up report assessing durability of the original 2022 pilot's changes.

author_or_institution: Alda (Association for Democracy and Sustainability) and Autonomy Institute
title: Going Public: Iceland's Journey to a Shorter Working Week
claim_or_use: Iceland's 2015-2019 public-sector trials (66 workplaces, about 2,500 workers): reduced hours without pay cuts did not reduce productivity, and 86% of Iceland's workforce subsequently gained shorter hours or the right to shorten them
notes: Co-published by an Icelandic and a British research organization; covers Reykjavik City Council and Icelandic government trials specifically.

title: Iceland embraced a shorter work week. Here's how it turned out
claim_or_use: Follow-up economic context: Iceland's GDP growth (4.1% in 2023) and low unemployment (3.6%) cited alongside the shorter-week trials, with appropriate caution against over-attributing macroeconomic outcomes to the labor policy alone
notes: Used for context and explicitly flagged in-text as correlational, not causal, macroeconomic evidence.

title: Valve Handbook for New Employees
claim_or_use: Documented details of Valve's flat structure ('nobody reports to anybody else'), desks on wheels enabling self-organized project teams, and 100%-self-directed project selection
notes: Leaked and later semi-officially distributed internal handbook; a first-party document describing intended structure, not an independent audit of lived experience.

title: Valve's unusual corporate structure causes its problems
claim_or_use: Journalism
url: Documented criticism of Valve's flat structure, including internal status hierarchies and clique formation despite the absence of formal management
notes: https://www.pcgamer.com/valves-unusual-corporate-structure-causes-its-problems-report-suggests/
column11: Used deliberately as counter-evidence to the idealized reading of the Valve handbook.

title: Netflix Culture: Freedom and Responsibility
claim_or_use: Netflix's 2009 culture deck: 'freedom and responsibility,' 'context not control,' the 'keeper test,' and unlimited vacation policy, later described by Sheryl Sandberg as an unusually influential Silicon Valley document
notes: Wikipedia entry used to confirm dating, authorship, and reception details of the original SlideShare deck (which by 2026 had accumulated over 15 million views).

title: Is Netflix's 2009 Culture Deck Still Relevant Today To Shape Company Culture?
claim_or_use: Retrospective assessment of the Netflix culture deck's influence and its later, more institutionalized and criticized form inside Netflix itself
notes: Used for the chapter's counter-evidence on how 'freedom and responsibility' was later experienced as high-pressure by some employees.

title: It's one of the biggest experiments in fighting global poverty. Now
claim_or_use: Public radio journalism
url: Reuse of the Kenya UBI enterprise-formation finding as evidence that income security and purposeful economic activity moved together rather than as a trade-off in the long-horizon arm
notes: https://www.npr.org/sections/goatsandsoda/2023/12/07/1217478771/its-one-of-the-biggest-experiments-in-fighting-global-poverty-now-the-results-ar
column11: Same source as ch12-004, revisited here for the book's synthesis argument about complements versus trade-offs.

title: Rising morbidity and mortality in midlife among white non-Hispanic Americans in the 21st century
claim_or_use: Reuse to argue that purpose loss carries material, not merely subjective, stakes
notes: Same source as ch15-001, revisited in the synthesis argument.

title: Bullshit Jobs: A Theory
claim_or_use: Argues a large share of jobs are subjectively experienced by their own holders as lacking meaningful social contribution, citing a YouGov survey finding 37% of UK workers believed their job made no meaningful contribution to the world
notes: Simon & Schuster, 2018. Cited alongside its academic critics (Soffia, Wood, and Burchell's empirical critique) rather than as an uncontested finding.

author_or_institution: Magdalena Soffia; Alex J. Wood; Brendan Burchell
title: Alienation Is Not 'Bullshit': An Empirical Critique of Graeber's Theory of BS Jobs
claim_or_use: Empirical critique finding considerably fewer than Graeber's suggested 20-60% of jobs are experienced as 'useless' when measured more precisely, with well under 10% of European workers reporting their job as useless in some surveys, and that figure declining rather than growing over time
notes: Work, Employment and Society. Used as counter-evidence tempering Graeber's more sweeping claims.

title: How Company Culture Shapes Employee Motivation
claim_or_use: Closing reuse of the total-motivation framework to organize the book's practical synthesis for individuals, managers, and policymakers
notes: Same source as ch03-001.

title: The Future of Jobs Report 2025
claim_or_use: Closing reuse of the net job-creation projection to keep the book's final chapter honest about genuine uncertainty rather than false closure
notes: Same source as ch08-001.
